entries.status_note: Fuel-limited free drift since leaving the 10:30 morning constellation: no maneuvers planned, equator crossing moving earlier (NASA: 9:06 MLT and 693 km as of Dec 2025). NASA plans Terra/Aqua shutdown in late 2026/early 2027. MODIS in nominal science mode as of 6 Nov 2026.
entries.acquisition_note: Global systematic acquisition; thermal bands also acquire on the night (ascending) node. Equator crossing time is no longer nominal (drifting earlier than the historical 10:30), so local illumination differs from the original design.
entries.spectral: 36 bands, ~0.41-14.2 um (2 bands 250 m, 5 bands 500 m, 29 bands 1 km)

entries.status_note: Free drift since the last drag-makeup maneuver in Dec 2021: descending below the A-Train, crossing time drifting later (WMO OSCAR: 15:05 ascending, record updated 2026-11-09). Earlier NASA plans ended Aqua MODIS science around Aug 2026, but MODIS is still in nominal science mode as of 6 Nov 2026; NASA states Terra/Aqua shutdown late 2026/early 2027.
entries.acquisition_note: Global systematic acquisition; thermal bands also acquire on the night (descending) node. Equator crossing time is no longer the nominal 13:30 and keeps drifting later.

entries.status_note: ASTER TIR subsystem permanently turned off on 16 Jan 2026 due to Terra power limitations; its thermal control was powered off on 6 Feb 2026, so it cannot be recovered. ASTER VNIR resumed on 9 Feb 2026 (SWIR non-functional since 2008).
entries.acquisition_note: Historical only: TIR archive ends 16 Jan 2026. When operating, ASTER acquired on a scheduled (tasked) basis with +/-8.55 deg cross-track pointing for TIR.

entries.status_note: Maintenance operation 18 Oct - 15 Nov 2026 (JST): nominal observations suspended, no new tasking, data non-calibrated. Late-phase operation: duty cycle reduced to 30%; observations restricted in some regions outside Japan (radio-interference countermeasures).
entries.acquisition_note: Basic Observation Scenario 4th ed.: global Stripmap 10 m given lower priority since ALOS-4 took over global mapping; ScanSAR 350 km continues for wetlands/deforestation, polar and crustal deformation; Japan mostly left-looking. Default mode = Fine F2 group (beams 5-7, 70 km each); one beam per pass, so the incidence range is an envelope of 3 beams.
entries.spectral: L-band; SP, DP (HH+HV / VV+VH), FP, experimental compact pol

entries.status_note: Regular operations since April 2025.
entries.acquisition_note: Basic Observation Scenario: global basemap in Stripmap 10 m (200 km, right, ascending, 1/yr) and Stripmap 6 m full-pol (100 km, descending); Japan in Stripmap 3 m (200 km). Check per-cycle PALSAR-3 observation plans (KML).
entries.spectral: L-band, digital beamforming

entries.status_note: Far beyond 5-year design life; WMO OSCAR (updated 2026-10-19) lists Operational, EOL >=2028 (estimated).

entries.spectral: X-band; single, dual (HH/VV, HH/HV, VV/VH) pol

entries.status_note: Flies in close formation with TerraSAR-X. DLR lists active (as of 2026); WMO OSCAR (updated 2026-10-19) EOL >=2028 (estimated).

entries.status_note: In service since 2018; operated in constellation with TerraSAR-X/TanDEM-X. Successor PAZ-2 expected ~2031.
entries.acquisition_note: Commercial tasking (Hisdesat; marketed with TerraSAR-X/TanDEM-X by Airbus). StripMap 30 km single pol (15 km dual), ScanSAR 100 km, SpotLight 10 km. Access incidence 15-60 deg; full-performance 20-45 deg (StripMap, TerraSAR-X heritage). Nominal right-looking; left-looking attitude possible.
entries.spectral: X-band; single and dual pol

entries.status_note: Extended mission since 2024, 'through at least 2026'. New acquisitions still being delivered (LP DAAC alert, 17 Sep 2026). Invited to the 2026 NASA Earth Science Senior Review (FY2027-FY2029); outcome not found.
entries.acquisition_note: Prime mission targeted arid dust-source regions (Africa, Asia, Americas, Australia). The extended mission adds other targets (greenhouse-gas sources, vegetation, snow, inland waters). Planned acquisitions are published as ~2-week forecasts on the EMIT data portal; the on-board cloud screener may drop scenes.
entries.spectral: Imaging spectrometer 380-2500 nm, 285 bands, ~7.4 nm sampling

entries.status_note: NASA Earthdata (22 Sep 2026): 'Both ECOSTRESS and OCO-3 are currently operating on the ISS'. Five-band-only mode since 18 May 2023. 2026 Senior Review (FY2027-FY2029) proposal presented Apr 2026; outcome not found.
entries.acquisition_note: Targeted acquisitions (originally CONUS, twelve 1000x1000 km climate zones and 25 Fluxnet sites; ~230 scenes/day in 2026). Day and night.
entries.spectral: TIR radiometer, 5 bands 8.29-12.09 um (five-band mode since May 2023)

entries.status_note: Status in 2026 unclear: latest DLR statement (Apr 2025) says seven years of operations completed; WMO OSCAR (updated 2 Feb 2026) lists it operational, EOL >=2026. No 2026 operations report or end-of-mission notice found.
entries.acquisition_note: Tasked via DLR science proposals (>=2000 min/year) or TBE commercially; not intended for large-area mapping. MUSES pointing across-track -45 to +5 deg (asymmetric, modelled here as +/-45 deg), along-track +/-40 deg.
entries.spectral: VNIR imaging spectrometer 402-1000 nm, 235 bands (2.55 nm) unbinned

entries.status_note: Inferred end of operations ~March 2026: JAXA Kibo weekly schedule of 22 Dec 2025 lists HISUI among ongoing exposed-facility payloads; the schedule of 3 Mar 2026 no longer does and shows 'HISUI in-cabin cleanup' on 5 Mar 2026. eoPortal gives EOL 31 Mar 2026 ('Mission complete'). WMO OSCAR (2 Feb 2026) still listed it operational. No formal end-of-mission announcement found.
entries.acquisition_note: Request-based targeting with limited downlink; most data returned on recorder media.
entries.spectral: Imaging spectrometer 0.4-2.5 um, 185 bands (10 nm VNIR, 12.5 nm SWIR)

entries.status_note: Routine phase since 2 Nov 2022; nominal mission to 2027, DLR intends to continue. enmap.org news active up to 10 Nov 2026.
entries.acquisition_note: User-ordered observations plus a Foreground Mission over Europe. Winter mode Nov 2026-Feb 2027: Europe imaged only south of the Alps, focus shifts to the Southern Hemisphere. Cloud-forecast filtering in planning.
entries.spectral: VNIR 420-1000 nm + SWIR 900-2450 nm, >240 bands

entries.status_note: Beyond 5-year design life; eoPortal 'Operational (extended)'. Latest ASI status found is May 2025 (workshop presentation); no 2026 status statement found. Successor PRISMA Second Generation planned ~2031.
entries.acquisition_note: User-driven on-demand acquisitions (registration, free of charge, quota/priority) plus a monthly Foreground Mission of 668 sites and background fill. Mission access limited to 70S-70N.

entries.acquisition_note: Six beams in three strong/weak pairs; pair tracks ~3.3 km apart, beams within a pair ~90 m apart. Pointing follows per-91-day-cycle pointing plans (reference ground tracks over the ice sheets, plus off-pointing campaigns, e.g. Cycle 33, 12 Sep - 12 Dec 2026: land-ice off-pointing for RGTs 1-598 until 21 Oct 2026), so actual beam tracks can be offset from the TLE-predicted nadir. Laser profiling works day and night.
entries.spectral: Photon-counting laser altimeter (532 nm)

entries.status_note: Status unclear for Nov 2026. Re-installed at its original ISS location in Apr 2024 after storage (17 Mar 2023 - Apr 2024); NASA Earthdata instrument page says 'Operational' and CEOS lists 'Operational (extended)', EOL Sep 2029. But the latest released acquisitions end on 10 Jul 2025 (V3 release notice, updated 22 Oct 2026) and no source says whether collection continued after that date. Outcome of NASA's 2026 Earth Science Senior Review for GEDI not found.
entries.acquisition_note: Three lasers produce 8 ground tracks spaced ~600 m across-track (~4.2 km total), footprints every 60 m along-track; the track offsets here are derived from that spacing. The instrument can be pointed up to ~40 km either side of the ISS ground track, so actual tracks may be offset. Coverage limited to 51.6N-51.6S.
entries.spectral: Full-waveform laser altimeter (1064 nm)

entries.status_note: Operational in the 21-day repeat science orbit (OSCAR, updated Apr 2026).
entries.acquisition_note: Ka-band radar interferometer: two parallel swaths (~50 km each) either side of a ~20 km nadir gap; the gap is covered only by the separate nadir altimeter. Day and night, all weather.
entries.spectral: Ka-band SAR interferometer

entries.agency: EUMETSAT / ESA / NASA / NOAA / European Commission (CNES support)
entries.status_note: Current reference altimetry mission. Sentinel-6B (launched 17 Nov 2025) flies in tandem ~30 s behind for cross-calibration and will take over the reference role; Sentinel-6 MF is then planned to move its ground track to interleave with Sentinel-6B. Date of that move not confirmed as of Nov 2026 (TLE-based prediction stays valid, but the repeat ground track will change).
entries.acquisition_note: Nadir-only radar altimeter, no imaging swath. footprint_m is the SAR-mode along-track resolution (~300 m); the cross-track pulse-limited footprint is much larger (km scale). Day and night, all weather.
entries.spectral: Ku/C-band SAR radar altimeter

entries.status_note: Operating in extended mission (ESA operational news May 2026). ESA mission page still says 'extended to 2025'; OSCAR (Jan 2026): extension to 2028 proposed; CPOM: extended until 2028.
entries.acquisition_note: Nadir-only radar altimeter; LRM, SAR and SARIn modes selected by target area (geographical mode mask). footprint_m is the SAR-mode along-track resolution (~250 m); the cross-track footprint is km scale. Orbit drifts through all local times. Day and night.
entries.spectral: Ku-band SAR/interferometric radar altimeter

entries.status_note: Sentinel-3C was launched on 15 Sep 2026; it will initially operate alongside Sentinel-3A/3B and eventually take over from Sentinel-3A (date not stated).
entries.acquisition_note: Nadir-only radar altimeter with no swath: one range measurement across-track per pulse. Operates 100% in SAR mode (~300 m along-track resolution, used as footprint_m). Day and night.
entries.spectral: Ku/C-band SAR radar altimeter

entries.acquisition_note: Nadir-only radar altimeter with no swath: one range measurement across-track per pulse. Operates 100% in SAR mode (~300 m along-track resolution, used as footprint_m). Day and night.
entries.spectral: Ku/C-band SAR radar altimeter

entries.status_note: Metop-B is still operational (EUMETSAT, updated 5 Nov 2026), but AVHRR/3 near-visible channels 1, 2 and 3A have been degraded since July 2023 and are all out of SNR specification (OSCAR).
entries.acquisition_note: Global, continuous. IR channels image day and night; visible/NIR channels only on daylit (descending, ~09:00 LT) passes.
Global, continuous. IR channels image day and night; visible/NIR channels only on daylit (descending, ~09:30 LT) passes.

entries.status_note: Metop-SGA1 is still in commissioning (EUMETSAT, updated 5 Nov 2026). METimage level-1 processor released to direct-broadcast users on 2 Sep 2026 (patch 5 Oct 2026); NWP SAF expects all instruments to finish commissioning ~18 months after launch (early 2027). Data not yet operational.
entries.acquisition_note: Global, continuous whisk-broom imager (+/-54 deg). IR channels image day and night; reflective channels only on daylit (descending, ~09:30 LT) passes.
entries.spectral: 20 channels, 443 nm - 13.345 um

entries.status_note: NOAA permanently ceased delivery of all S-NPP science data (VIIRS, ATMS, CERES, OMPS) on 2 Nov 2026 (ended 15:40 UTC per NASA Earthdata) and disabled direct broadcast; users told to move to NOAA-21/NOAA-20. OSCAR marks the satellite inactive (VIIRS EOL 1 Nov 2026). The spacecraft still has current GP data on CelesTrak.
entries.acquisition_note: Global, continuous. The Day/Night Band (0.5-0.9 um) and the IR bands image at night, so both the daytime ascending (~13:30 LT) and night-time descending passes are useful; reflective bands only by day. No new data after 2 Nov 2026.
entries.spectral: 22 bands 0.41-12.0 um incl. Day/Night Band

entries.status_note: Secondary JPSS afternoon satellite (NOAA-21 is primary).
entries.acquisition_note: Global, continuous. The Day/Night Band (0.5-0.9 um) and the IR bands image at night, so both the daytime ascending (~13:30 LT) and night-time descending passes are useful; reflective bands only by day.

entries.status_note: Satellite and TROPOMI performing well; operations secured until end of 2027, extension under discussion. Loose formation with Suomi-NPP ends by Q4 2026 (ESA, May 2026).
entries.acquisition_note: Daylight measurements only (UV-VIS-NIR-SWIR spectrometer); full daily coverage poleward of 7 deg latitude, >95% between 7S and 7N.

entries.status_note: Metop-SGA1 still in commissioning (EUMETSAT, 5 Nov 2026). EUMETSAT plan (May 2026): ESA-to-EUMETSAT handover from Aug 2026, L1 and first L2 products late summer 2026, remaining L2 in Q4 2026, SWIR products (CO, CH4) possibly later. Actual product release status in Nov 2026 not confirmed.
entries.acquisition_note: Daylight measurements only (UV-VIS-NIR-SWIR spectrometer), descending morning orbit (~09:30 LT).

entries.status_note: Prime operational satellite at 0 deg (full disc every 10 min) since June 2025; Meteosat-10 runs in parallel at 0 deg until ~Q2 2027. The 2.5-min rapid scan over Europe is to come from MTG-I2 (launched 27 Aug 2026, in commissioning; EUMETSAT: 'from end 2026'). EUMETSAT reports loss of the FCI on-board calibration source, mitigated with IASI-referenced IR calibration.
entries.acquisition_note: Full disc (Europe, Africa, Atlantic) every 10 min, day and night (IR); reflective channels by day only.

swath.rapid_scan_note: No rapid scan from Meteosat-12. Europe RSS (2.5 min) planned from MTG-I2 from end 2026; the MSG 5-min RSS continues from Meteosat-11 at 9.5E.

entries.spectral: 16 channels 0.44-13.3 um

entries.status_note: At 0 deg providing the MSG 0-deg full-disc SEVIRI service (15 min) in parallel with Meteosat-12 (prime) until ~Q2 2027, then backup to Meteosat-12 (OSCAR). Temporary mission swap with Meteosat-11 on 24-28 Apr 2026; nominal 0-deg service from Meteosat-10 resumed 28 Apr 2026. CelesTrak GP data show ~5.0 deg inclination, so the sub-satellite point oscillates N-S by about +/-5 deg daily.
entries.acquisition_note: Full disc every 15 min, day and night (IR); reflective channels by day only.
entries.spectral: 12 channels (11 narrow-band 0.6-13.4 um + HRV)

entries.status_note: At 9.5E providing the MSG Rapid Scanning Service (Europe and North Africa every 5 min) since 22 Mar 2023; also full-disc backup. Temporarily ran full-disc mode 24-28 Apr 2026; RSS from Meteosat-11 resumed 28 Apr 2026.
entries.acquisition_note: Rapid scan only: imaging limited to the northern part of the disc (Europe and North Africa); no full-disc images in nominal operations. IR day and night, reflective channels by day only.

swath.rapid_scan_note: Operates in RSS mode: repeat_min is the 5-min rapid-scan cycle over Europe/North Africa, not a full-disc repeat.

entries.spectral: 12 channels (11 narrow-band 0.6-13.4 um + HRV)

entries.status_note: Operating in 2026 (ESA Level-2 operational processor update 8 Sep 2026). ESA mission page still says operations 'till 2025' and OSCAR gives EOL >=2026; a formal extension beyond 2025 was not found.
